title: Stereotactic and Palliative Radiotherapy for Metastatic Ovarian Cancer: Analysis of Treatment Response and Clinical Outcomes
summary:
Background:
In advanced ovarian cancer, primary treatment consists of surgery and systemic therapy (chemotherapy). However, radiation therapy is gaining importance to relieve symptoms, control local tumor sites, and extend the time before the next chemotherapy line is needed.

Research Question:
This study evaluates the effectiveness and safety of stereotactic and palliative radiation therapy in patients with metastatic ovarian cancer.

Methodology:
This is a retrospective data analysis. Medical records, radiation plans, and diagnostic imaging of patients treated at the radiation oncology department between January 1990 and July 2026 will be analyzed. Key parameters evaluated include treatment response, survival outcomes, and both acute and late side effects. Patient data are evaluated retrospectively without requiring additional hospital visits.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of other and unspecified female genital organs
Malignant neoplasm of retroperitoneum and peritoneum

interventions.name: Patients with metastatic or oligoprogressive ovarian cancer who have received stereotactic or palliative radiotherapy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with histologically confirmed epithelial ovarian cancer (including fallopian tube/peritoneal cancer).
Undergoing radiotherapy (in the timeframe from January 1990 to June 2026 )
Exclusion criteria:
Incomplete clinical or radiotherapy documentation data that makes reliable endpoint evaluation impossible
